meaning:
ἄ-μωμος, -ον
(μῶμος, which see), [in LXX chiefly for תָּמִים ];
of sacrificial victims, without blemish: of Christ, Heb.9:14, 1Pe.1:19; etbically, unblemished, faultless: Eph.1:4 5:27, Php.2:15, Col.1:22, Ju 24, Rev.14:5 (Cremer, 425, 788; MM, VGT, see word).†
SYN.: ἀμίαντος, ἄσπιλος (AS)

elsewhere.note: even as he chose us in him before the foundation of the world, that we would be holy and without defect before him in love,
that you may become blameless and harmless, children of God without defect in the middle of a crooked and perverse generation, among whom you are seen as…
yet now he has reconciled in the body of his flesh through death, to present you holy and without defect and blameless before him,
how much more will the blood of Christ, who through the eternal Spirit offered himself without defect to God, cleanse your conscience from dead works to serve…
but with precious blood, as of a lamb without blemish or spot, the blood of Christ,
Now to him who is able to keep them from stumbling, and to present you faultless before the presence of his glory in great joy,
In their mouth was found no lie, for they are blameless.
